A1.justification: Both complete 38-page PDFs describe the same AutoSafe/OTS research despite the changed title. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original safety experiments on SEDA and ToolEmu, evaluation on 32 real-world cases, and supplementary evaluator, trajectory and fine-grained analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and outcomes, including Tables 1–6 and the empirical analyses in the appendices.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same risk-scenario generation, reflective safe-action sampling and fine-tuning procedure. The simulator highlighted by the new title already appears in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same SEDA and ToolEmu coverage, 32 real-world cases, unseen-risk scenarios, four task domains and ten risk categories. No training or evaluation coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged, including the model rosters and Baseline, Naive and Reflection comparisons in Tables 1–2, and the voting evaluator in Appendix A.3. AgentPoison is newly cited but not evaluated.

E3.justification: The 50-scenario test sets, training-data construction, sec@1/3/5 evaluation, real-world testing procedure and Table 12 settings remain unchanged, including the five-epoch LoRA configuration.

E4.justification: Both retain the same unseen-risk comparisons, fine-grained safety analyses, cost and utility checks, evaluator validation, trajectory analysis in Appendix E.4 and case studies in Appendix G.

E5.justification: Plot error bars and Table 6's Cohen's kappa reporting with ± values are unchanged. v2 adds no run-count or seed disclosures, uncertainty procedures or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted findings and qualitative examples are unchanged throughout both PDFs. For example, Table 2's GLM-9B ToolEmu Sec@1 under Ours remains 78.0%, and Table 3's corresponding real-world score remains 71.9%.

T1.justification: The OTS definitions, Equations (1)–(14) and Definition 1 in Appendix A.3 are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: Despite retitling, the abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and novelty claims concerning OTS, automated safety-data generation and safety improvement, including the claimed 45.4% average improvement.

C2.justification: Interpretations of generalization, safety versus utility and evaluator reliability remain unchanged. Appendix F retains the qualification that the contribution concerns automated data generation rather than new safety-training algorithms.

D1.justification: Appendices A, D and H retain the same component details, hyperparameters and full prompts. The project-page link and code/data access information are unchanged; no reproducibility details are added.

R1.justification: v2 adds AgentPoison: Red-teaming LLM agents via poisoning memory or knowledge bases as reference 37 and cites it in Section 5's existing agent-safety discussion. The surrounding positioning is unchanged; subsequent references are renumbered.

P1.justification: The title changes from Automating Safety Enhancement for LLM-based Agents with Synthetic Risk Scenarios to SafeAgent: Safeguarding LLM Agents via an Automated Risk Simulator. The abstract and body continue to use AutoSafe. Section organization and substantive prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The citation addition causes limited reflow in Section 5 and shifts subsequent bibliography entries on page 12. All 14 figures and 12 tables retain their displays, captions, structure and placement.

improvement.justification: The experiments, analyses, limitations and reproducibility material are unchanged. The AgentPoison citation provides a small acknowledgment benefit, while the new SafeAgent title remains unreconciled with AutoSafe in the text. These limited editorial changes leave overall paper quality essentially unchanged.
